title: Landry Shamet agrees to return to Knicks on 4-year, $24 million deal
content:
Landry Shamet intends to sign a four-year, $24 million deal to return to the New York Knicks, league sources who spoke anonymously because the deal has not yet been finalized confirmed to The Athletic.

Shamet’s 3-point shooting and on-ball defense were instrumental to New York’s title run this season. The eight-year veteran made 18 of 24 3s between the Eastern Conference semifinals and Eastern Conference finals.

The 29-year-old guard has played the last two seasons on a minimum contract and was in a three-way battle last training camp for the final roster spot. Shamet quickly earned the trust of head coach Mike Brown and became a fixture in the Knicks’ rotation.

The Knicks have thought highly of Shamet since he arrived in New York in 2024. During each of his two seasons with the team, Shamet suffered a shoulder injury that forced him to miss substantial time. Yet even though he was on a minimum deal, the Knicks never released him.

Shamet was expected to garner interest from other teams, per league sources, but he valued his time with the Knicks and chose to return.

He is expected to be New York’s biggest offseason move this year. Knicks owner James Dolan said publicly that he doesn’t want his team to go into the second apron. Unless Dolan changes his tune or New York makes an unexpected trade, the mandate to keep spending below the second apron makes it unlikely that the team will bring back free-agent center Mitchell Robinson.

Assuming Robinson is gone, the Knicks must now add a cheap center and another veteran-minimum player to fill out the 14-player roster.
